newsitem.title: USA: Mondex says CyberCash in development deal.
newsitem.headline: Mondex says CyberCash in development deal.

text.p: SAN FRANCISCO, Sept 25 (Reuter) Mondex International Ltd announced a joint development accord with CyberCash Inc to integrate the CyberCash Wallet along with other global payment brands for use with its Mondex smart card technology.

Mondex, which is headquartered in London and owned by 17 companies spanning four continents, said the collaboration would allow Mondex card holders to use their cards to purchase goods over the Internet in a secure and convenient manner.
"This Internet compatibility will enable Mondex smart cards to bridge the physical and virtual worlds," the organization said in a statement released here.

The combination of the two technologies will allow the smart card, used with a PC-linked reader, to be used for online transactions between consumers, merchants and banks, as well as for consumer-to-consumer transactions.

The technology also allows low-cost online purchases expected to be at the core of future electronic commerce and allow card carriers to credit funds to their cards across the Internet global computer network.

"This partnership represents a major step forward in making Mondex the worldwide alternative to cash, both for the supermarket and the superhighway," said Richard Fletcher, head of Strategy and Planning, Mondex International Ltd.
Mondex is being launched in Britain by a joint venture of National Westminster Bank and Midland Bank working with British Telecommunications Plc.
In the U.S., Mondex is being introduced by Wells Fargo Bank and AT&T Universal Card Services.
